answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a resource bond before it may transact: an agent locks a deposit, and reputation accrues only through completed work over time, so no newcomer instantly reaches the zenith of trust. Like quartz forming under pressure, standing builds slowly and cannot be faked at scale. An attacker spinning up an island of fake identities must fund a bond for every one and repeat the costly work history for each, so forgery costs grow linearly while an honest agent pays once. Slashing the bond on proven fraud turns each fake into a net loss.
